title: Data-driven reduced modeling of neural dynamics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75924-7

Spectral submanifolds can be used to reduce recurrent neural networks to low-dimensional models, revealing their core dynamics. Here, authors uncover robust structures underlying decision-making and working-memory tasks, providing predictions about the underlying behavior of neural computations.

title: Tailoring d–p orbital hybridization of single-atom Cu-N2S sites for enhanced photo-Fenton reaction
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76057-7

In this study, the authors report that asymmetric Cu–N2S coordination enables robust photo-Fenton activity for pollutant degradation over a broad pH range, driven by d–p hybridization and an anti-band-center effect that boost H2O2 activation.

title: Interacting non-Hermitian edge and cluster bursts on a digital quantum processor
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75904-x

Using digital quantum simulators to study non-Hermitian physics requires realizing non-unitary time-evolution on unitary gate-based hardware. Here, the authors tackle this issue using an ancilla-assisted circuit block performing controlled forward and backward Hermitian time-evolution, and simulate multi-particle non-Hermitian edge burst on superconducting transmon-based quantum hardware.

title: Skeletal muscle properties in long COVID and ME/CFS differ from those induced by bed rest
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75725-y

Low aerobic capacity in patients with long COVID and ME/CFS is often attributed to physical inactivity. The authors show that long COVID and ME/CFS patients have distinct skeletal muscle changes that cannot be solely explained by physical inactivity.

title: Iron deficiency strategy toward single-phase high-entropy M-type ferrites for broadband millimeter-wave absorption with low thickness
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76164-5

Single-phase high-entropy M-type ferrites have been synthesized successfully via an iron deficiency strategy, achieving a broad millimeter-wave absorption bandwidth of 12.18 GHz around 35 GHz with thickness below 1 mm.

title: Insights into the mechanisms of NH<sub>3</sub> inhibition on Cu-CHA SCR catalysts
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72879-7

Selective catalytic reduction (SCR) of nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) using ammonia (NH₃) over small-pore Cu-zeolites is a key technology for mitigating NOₓ emissions from lean-burn engines. Here, the authors clarify the atomic-scale mechanism responsible for ammonia inhibition during NOₓ SCR on Cu-CHA catalysts.

title: Food-related energy consumption can help reveal poverty in rural Chinese households
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76026-0

This study introduces the Energy Engel Coefficient, a food-related energy consumption indicator. Using household survey data from China, it identifies low-income rural households not identified by traditional income-based poverty measures.

title: Enantioselective synthesis of ring-constrained biaryls via a twist-expand-seal strategy
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76125-y

The authors report a “twist-expand-seal” strategy for synthesizing a unique class of cyclic biaryls that exhibit axial chirality and conformational constraint, with adjustable ring sizes.
